text:
Asha: hi team, first rotation today — quick question before i ack anything: i tried creating a maintenance window to quiet a noisy test alert but PD rejects it with 'insufficient permissions'. i'm worried i'll accidentally silence the whole service if i get perms wrong. who can approve a scoped maintenance window?
Ben: welcome Asha! you shouldn't be able to silence everything unless you're an Admin. for scoped windows we use the "service" dropdown in PD and select the specific service (e.g., search-api). what error exactly did you get?
Asha: the modal says: "You do not have permission to create a maintenance window for this schedule. Contact your admin." clicked "Create for service" -> service: search-api -> scope: all incidents -> submit -> rejected.
Liam: sounds like PD role mapping is missing the "Maintenance Creator" permission for your Responder role. @Ben can you check the PD role rules? also, quick tip: if you need a temporary quiet for tests, use the incident simulator or create a maintenance window with very narrow scope and short duration (10 min) to avoid broad impact.
Ben: checking PD roles... your account has Responder but not the "maintenance" capability. i'll add a role exception for the onboarding week so you can create scoped windows capped at 15m. doing that now.
ops-bot: Access Control  Role adjustment: Asha (asha@redwood.ai) granted temporary permission maintenance:create with expiry 2026-04-10T12:00:00Z. Please exercise caution when creating maintenance windows.
Asha: thanks! one more question: is there a canonical checklist for maintenance windows? i want to include the right summary and not disrupt downstream teams.
Liam: yep — short checklist: 1) scope to service(s) not entire schedule, 2) add summary prefixed with [MAINT-ONBOARDING], 3) set duration <= 15m for tests, 4) set 'Notify' to only the test group, 5) add linked runbook or PR number in details. I'll DM you the snippet we paste into the summary.
Ben: adding the permission now. try creating a window and set scope to only search-api:read-only or the specific alert rule id. if you want i can watch and confirm it only silences the test alert.
Asha: created a 10m window with summary: "[MAINT-ONBOARDING] test alert suppression - follow runbook #423" and scope search-api:read-only. modal accepted and the test alert stopped firing. thanks!
oncall-bot: Incident Simulator  Maintenance window created by Asha: 2026-04-05T18:30Z -> 2026-04-05T18:40Z, scope: search-api:read-only.
Asha: phew, that worked. last tiny worry: what if an actual sev2 happens while a maintenance window is active? does PD still escalate?
Liam: maintenance windows suppress alerts for matching rules but we have an override policy for sev1/2 critical incidents — if an alert has severity >= sev2 and matches the critical tag, PD will still page the escalation policy. in other words, maintenance won't hide a true critical. also the runbook has a section "emergency-override" describing how to manually cancel a window: `pd maintenance cancel <id>` or via the UI.
Ben: added a short note to the onboarding checklist and flagged ops to review the temporary permission after your rotation. enjoy the sim later — i'll be there to watch the first few operations.
Asha: awesome, thanks everyone :rocket: appreciate the help and the safety net on perms.
